notes: rust_stdlib::expvar: Var (a trait whose Display output is valid JSON), Int and Float (atomic; Float.Add is a compare-exchange loop on the bits), String, Map (sorted keys; Map::add and add_float recognize Int and Float through Var::as_int and Var::as_float, the Rust form of Go's type assertion), Func, publish/get/iter and the published constructors over a process-wide registry. JSON rendering follows expvar's own quoting (appendJSONQuote), the expanded layout of the handler, and encoding/json (json::marshal) for Func. tests/expvar.rs ports expvar_test.go (the handler and quoting tables included); tools/expvar_check.py runs 400 seeded scripts (7,395 operation records) against Go, comparing every rendered value and duplicate-name panic exactly.

Do.note: Calls f for each published variable in name order over a snapshot of the registry. Go holds the registry lock while f runs, so publishing a new variable from f blocks forever there; here it returns (see Map.Do).

Float.String.note: The Display rendering: Go's strconv 'g' format with the shortest exact digits.

Func.note: Go's Func returns any and json.Marshal renders it, including reflection on arbitrary Go values. The Rust Func returns a json::Value, which cannot hold NaN or Inf: Go renders those as an empty string because json.Marshal fails, and the port cannot reproduce that case.

Func.String.note: json::marshal (Go's HTML-escaping encoder) of the value; an encoding failure is the empty string.

Func.Value.note: Returns a json::Value instead of any; see Func.

Get.note: Returns None for a missing name, as Go's nil. The registry starts with cmdline (as Go's init does, on first use), but not memstats, which in Go reports runtime.MemStats; the port cannot express that runtime snapshot.

Handler.note: Returns a route for rust_stdlib::net::http::Router (available with the net feature) that writes the variables as Go's /debug/vars does, with the expanded layout and the JSON content type. Go's init also registers it on http.DefaultServeMux; the port has no default mux, so callers register it with Router::route.

KeyValue.note: Value is never absent in the port: a nil Var cannot be stored (see Map.Set).

Map.Add.note: Adds to the Int under the key, creating one if the key is absent; a value of another type is left unchanged, as in Go.

Map.AddFloat.note: Adds to the Float under the key, creating one if the key is absent; a value of another type is left unchanged.

Map.Do.note: Go holds the map's key lock while f runs, so adding or deleting a key from f blocks forever. The port calls f over a snapshot of the entries, so such calls return; updates to existing entries behave as in Go.

Map.Get.note: Returns None for an absent key (Go's nil Var).

Map.Init.note: Removes all keys and returns the map.

Map.Set.note: Go accepts a nil Var, which renders as null; the port needs a Var value.

Map.String.note: Non-expanded JSON, as Go's Map.String; the handler uses the expanded form.

Publish.note: Panics with Go's log.Panicln message ("Reuse of exported var name: NAME" with its newline) for a duplicate name. Go also writes that message through the log package.

String.note: A string variable; the Rust type is named String as in Go, so std::string::String is written in full inside the module.

String.String.note: The quoted JSON string (expvar's own escaping: <, >, &, U+2028 and U+2029 become \u escapes).

Var.note: Send + Sync, so variables can be shared between threads; as_int and as_float are the Rust form of Go's type assertions.
